videos.script: Lesson 5 declared variables and gave them values. This lesson asks what a variable holds before you give it anything. In Go the answer is never garbage, and never undefined. {{zero}} Every type has a zero value, and the program on screen prints the zero of eleven types. Some zero values are useful just as they are, and the standard library is built around that. {{iota}} Then constants. Go has no enum keyword. A block of constants and a counter called iota do the same job, and the standard library numbers the days of the week exactly that way. {{scope}} Last, scope. Every pair of braces is a block, and a name declared inside one can hide a name outside it. {{shadow}} That is where a classic bug lives. A function finds an error, keeps it in the wrong variable, and returns nil. It compiles, and go vet says nothing. By the end you can say what an unset variable holds, number a set of constants, and spot the colon-equals that hides a variable.
